result.title: Anchoring with Visual Evidence: Explicit Semantic Anchors for Joint Change Detection and Captioning
result.summary: Joint change detection and captioning seeks to localize changes and describe them from bi-temporal remote sensing images. A key challenge is translating dense visual evidence into the semantic conditions that guide description generation. We propose Explicit Semantic Anchors (ESA), a supervised interface that exposes entity presence, temporal appearance variation, and spatial extent. A prediction-guided readout combines visual features and predicted change probabilities, and three factor heads estimate the corresponding anchor activations. These activations guide generation through two complementary routes. The context route maps the three factor activations to three separate memory tokens, one per factor, and appends them to the dense visual memory, while the lexicon route produces an additive vocabulary bias at each decoding step. Dense visual memory remains available for spatial detail and information beyond the explicit factors. Anchor targets are derived from existing images and change annotations, requiring no additional anchor-level language annotation. At inference, all conditions are computed from the input image pair and the model's own predictions. Experiments on LEVIR-MCI and WHU-CDC show strong joint detection and captioning performance, supporting the use of supervised visual attributes as explicit conditions for change description generation.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 Explicit Semantic Anchors（ESA），用监督方式显式暴露实体存在、时序外观变化与空间范围三类锚点，经预测引导读出后以记忆 token 和词汇偏置两条路径条件化双时相遥感图像的联合变化检测与描述生成。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「将稠密视觉证据压缩为少量显式因子并注入生成」的接口，可供核查 LVR 中视觉证据筛选、latent 内容是否真正被答案使用以及视觉旁路/信息坍缩等问题，但任务本身不是推理期 latent 状态生成。
